title: WARTS AND ALL - IS THE TAVELO AROW RIDEABLE? FULL BUILD

takeaways.text: After his earlier rework of the PF86 shell, he measured its bore at about 40.94–40.97 mm and fitted a threaded-press Cybre BB, but warns that a DUB-size axle in a PF86 shell leaves very small bearings.
The seatpost was too tight in one frame and loose in another, and the clamp wedge had sharp, burred machined corners that bear on the post; he filed both the seat tube and the wedge to make them fit.
The fork steerer cannot be left any longer than supplied, and the stack is very low, about 1 cm below his TCR in his setup; he suggests larger riders who are not flexible avoid it.

32 mm tires on 23 mm internal rims fit with the rear as the limit; he estimates the front could take about 35 mm, but thinks 32 mm is about the rear maximum. These are his observations, not manufacturer figures.

The single-bolt saddle clamp slipped even at its 16 Nm limit with carbon paste, and he had no chainstay protector or rear brake-hose foam, so the chain slaps the stay and the hose rattles in the down tube.
Once the problems are fixed, it is a stiff, noisy race bike that is fun for an hour but harsh on his rough roads; he would prefer a sloping top tube with more exposed seatpost.

disclosure: Tavelo supplied the frames reviewed on the channel; he bought the Ultegra Di2 groupset. The 2024 video shows the original Arow frameset and does not say whether it matches the current Race or SL version.
summary: A full Ultegra Di2 build log and one-month ride review of an original Tavelo Arow frameset, including bottom-bracket, seatpost and routing problems.
